title: Enforcement and inspections during the January 2026 vehicular Safety Time-out
asked: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye asked what specific enforcement or inspection actions MOM took to ensure companies not only paused operations during the voluntary Safety Time-out from 13 to 27 January 2026 but also made concrete improvements to vehicular safety practices.
response: The Ministry of Manpower called the Safety Time-out after four vehicle-related workplace fatalities in December. Because it was voluntary, there were no inspections or enforcement actions; MOM and the WSH Council encouraged participation and issued advisories. MOM also conducts regular inspections in high-risk sectors, with around 500 inspections in January, three stop-work orders and five fines for vehicle-related breaches.

key_points.point: The Safety Time-out was called after four vehicle-related workplace fatalities in December.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: because of four vehicle-related workplace fatalities in December

key_points.point: The Safety Time-out was voluntary, so there were no inspections nor enforcement actions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: In line with the voluntary nature of the Safety Time-out, there were no inspections nor enforcement actions.

key_points.point: MOM and the WSH Council encouraged companies to participate through existing channels.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: MOM and the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council, through its existing channels, have encouraged companies to participate in the Safety Time-out.

key_points.point: WSH advisories were issued on learning points from recent incidents and safety practices to reinforce with workers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: They have also issued WSH advisories to guide companies on the key learning points from the recent incidents and the relevant safety practices to be reinforced with their workers.

key_points.point: MOM conducts regular inspections in high-risk sectors where vehicular hazards are present.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: MOM conducts regular inspections in the high-risk sectors where vehicular hazards are present.

key_points.point: Around 500 inspections were conducted in January.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: Around 500 inspections have been conducted in January.

key_points.point: Three stop-work orders and five fines were issued for vehicle-related breaches.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: Three stop-work orders and five fines were issued to companies and individuals for vehicle-related breaches.

key_points.point: Existing WSH guidelines on fatigue management recommend rest breaks and managing shift work.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: WSH guidelines on fatigue management, where rest breaks are recommended and the need to manage shift work as well

key_points.point: The Productivity Solutions Grant offers SMEs 50% funding up to a $30,000 cap.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we have the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) that small and medium enterprises can tap upon, where 50% of funding can be defrayed, for up to a cap of $30,000.

key_points.point: As at July 2025, about 1,000 companies adopted vehicle safety technologies via the PSG, with about $12.5 million dispensed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: as at July 2025, about 1,000 companies have adopted vehicle safety technologies via the PSG, and a total of about $12.5 million has been dispensed.

key_points.point: Driver status monitoring systems can detect driver fatigue.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: such as the driver status monitoring system, which detects driver fatigue.

key_points.point: The Minister said he could not see common trends or root causes in the December cases and urged awaiting final investigations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: I could not see any common trends or any root causes, per se.

key_points.point: On mandating technology, the Minister said a holistic and calibrated approach is taken.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: we take a holistic and calibrated approach to all the solutions as well as the situation that we have.

key_points.point: He said the aim is to avoid a Maslow's Hammer situation where every problem is treated as a nail.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
key_points.quote: what we want to try to avoid is having a Maslow's Hammer type of a situation

left_open: How companies' implementation of concrete vehicular safety improvements was verified during the voluntary Safety Time-out.
Whether there are further plans to manage drivers' fatigue beyond existing WSH guidelines.
Whether mandating adoption of vehicular safety technologies will be considered for higher-risk sectors.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered driver fatigue management, take-up of vehicle safety technology grants, and whether adoption should be mandated.
